findings.where: Screen 3 (Power) and screen 1: energy graph, power bar and Lift motion
findings.what: The graph's time axis (niceT) and the power bar's scale (niceScale) rescale to every speed, and every lift animates in about 3.3 s. So dragging the speed from 0.2 to 0.4 m/s doubles the power readout but leaves the line's slope (it always ends 71-89% across), the bar's length (always 65-100% full) and the load's pace on screen unchanged. The read sentence 'A faster lift draws a steeper line' and 'power is the slope' are not what he sees. Fix the time axis (for example 0-120 s) and the power scale across speeds, or keep the last lift as a ghost line and bar.

No screen ever names 'potential energy', 'kinetic energy' or the conservation of energy. They appear only in the explain, which a steps lesson does not show, yet the brief promises them and lesson 6 builds its ½Iω² on kinetic energy. Name them where the screens already show mgh and ½mv², and on screen 9 say the total stays the same.

findings.where: Screen 9 (Brake off): text and the line under the picture
findings.what: 'for any load' and 'whatever its mass' are said about a winch whose drum is drawn paying out, but they hold only for a free fall with nothing else turning. The screens never show the ignores note, so say the load falls freely with the drum and motor's spin left out.
'Newton's laws give F = ma and v² = u² + 2as' credits the steady-acceleration equation to Newton's laws, but it comes from the speed-time graph's slope and area, so split it into two sentences.
'That energy of motion is ½ × mass × speed²' is stated without its why (the explain has it from F = ma and v² = 2as); one sentence on screen would close the step before screen 10 asks him to use it.
The text never says the 4905 J is the 500 kg load's weight × 1 m. The load also freezes in mid-air after a 13 px drop with no words saying the picture stops it there.

'The bars stand half as tall' describes horizontal bars (half as long). The supply power halves to 613 W only because the efficiency is held at 80%, which this screen should say, since a real motor's efficiency changes at half speed.
'And 19.62 ÷ 30 is the same 65.4%' makes the match look like chance. One sentence regrouping (load × lift) ÷ (effort × chain) into (load ÷ effort) ÷ (chain ÷ lift) would show why.

findings.where: Screen 11 (A chain block) first two sentences
findings.what: 'keeps the same ledger by hand' uses 'ledger' for the first time with no introduction, and 'When 30 m of hand chain is pulled with 250 N' is passive. 'Pull 30 m of hand chain with 250 N and a 500 kg load rises 1 m' reads better.
The why says the moment 'shares the newton metre', but no screen says a joule is a newton moved through a metre (only the explain and practice do), so screen 1 should say it once.
'Work is the area under a force-distance graph', promised as a recall of Calculus fundamentals lesson 9, appears neither on the screens nor in the explain.

Each opens with the set-up and reaches its point late: work in sentence four, the same energy at half the power after five sentences, efficiency in sentence four. Leading with the point would read better.

'lifts a load on a hook through an example 10 m' reads awkwardly. 'lifts a load 10 m; the height, the 80% efficiency and the puzzles' numbers are all examples' says the same thing plainly, written as two sentences.
'10 J' is the only answer not in watts for a power question, so he can rule it out by its unit alone; offer it as '10 W' with the same hint.
The right answer sits in the middle on five of the eight puzzles, a pattern he could learn, so vary its position.
It shows '981.0 W' while the words say 981 W; drop the trailing .0 when the value is whole.
The lesson column sits left-aligned in the wide card and leaves the right 45% empty; centre the 34rem column.
